limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation.
Original typed source inventory is not normalized; retain source identities and limits in the procedure/readsets.

applicability.scope: Diagnose vLLM-Ascend ACLGraph eligibility, capture/replay dispatch, caller-buffer ownership and capture-resource failures.
applicability.prerequisites: An existing eager correctness baseline; authorization before any new run or live configuration change.
applicability.input_contract: Installed stack and device, requested/effective graph mode, runner/backend settings, capture sizes and batch descriptors, error phase, replay observations and HBM/stream evidence.
applicability.produced_artifact: A bounded diagnosis, smallest reversible proposal, expected tradeoff and correctness/resource verification plan with unresolved compatibility or authorization questions.
applicability.refusal_point: Stop on output mismatch, unstable replay addresses, capture exhaustion, unknown ordering or version drift; missing evidence permits only a conditional proposal.

recommendations: Diagnose the effective runtime mode and batch descriptor before changing capture sizes; intended warmup/profile bypass is not a cache defect.
Trace stable replay buffers to the owning caller and preserve synchronization/update ordering; the wrapper does not stage new inputs into persistent buffers.
Compare eager and graph execution on the same workload, separating initial capture, repeated replay, compiler changes and memory/stream costs; a replay log alone proves neither coverage nor speedup.
